sources.notes: NIST Engineering Design Model Repository (1990s NIST parts repository): README calls it a public-domain collection; LICENSE.md is NIST 17 USC 105 terms. Caveat: models originated with 1990s industrial collaborators (PTC, SDRC, Parasolid, ICEM, CMU, Sandia...), NIST asserts public domain; operator may want to note provenance. 2411 STEP files, mostly ACIS STEP Husk, ST-Developer, Pro/ENGINEER, I-DEAS.

NIST page: 'The test cases, CAD models, and STEP files can be used without any restrictions' (acknowledgement requested). STEP from NIST-PMI-STEP-Files.zip, FTC/CTC definitions, FTC-CTC CAD-models zip and D2MI-Models zip. CAD system names deliberately stripped from headers (README), so producer is 'commercial-anonymised' (CATIA/Creo/NX/SolidWorks/Inventor + CoreTechnologie). Native CAD-only zips (STC v4, HTC, MTC assembly) contain no STEP.
NIST tooling parts, Inventor 2025/2026 AP214.

sources.version: Zenodo record 3975286 v1 (2020-08-06), CAD_Datasets_StandardPartClasses.zip 871265078 bytes; sample of 6 STEP per class (tools/sample_listing.py)
sources.notes: CC0 on the record. Variant models are NC State ISE 589 student homework parts built in Fusion 360 (product names such as HW7, TagHolder_DevavratM_HW7, McmasterDim_Externalretainer; ATF + ST-Developer headers; .f3d masters with user parameters), deposited by the course PI (bstarly) as CC0. 4,254 STEP in an 871 MB zip of parametric variants; deterministic sample = first 6 STEP per class directory in byte-wise sorted member order (tools/sample_listing.py, dl/mvcnn-sample.lst; 262 files, 56.7 MB), fetched with HTTP range requests (tools/remote_zip_get.py). The three Raw Data files are McMaster-Carr catalogue models and are excluded. Six files have an empty DATA section (kept as edge cases).
